judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic and pedagogy claims are all correct and I verified them independently: 27 ÷ 4 = 6 r3, 38 ÷ 5 = 7 r3, 6×7 + 3 = 45, 632 → 600 with 600 ÷ 8 = 75 (exact 79), 53 ÷ 8 = 6 r5 forcing 7 vans, 74 ÷ 9 = 8 r2, 145 ÷ 6 = 24 r1 via partial quotients, 87 ÷ 4 = 21 r3, 1347 → 1300 with 1300 ÷ 5 = 260 and the exact 269 r2, and 96 ÷ 7 = 13 r5. The eight study-guide values check too. The Quick Answers bank is complete and matches the key with no dropped rows. Two things the assessment misses. First, manual coverage: only problem 10 has a manual entry, but problem 8 prints 'Use the remainder rule to explain how you can tell she is wrong without dividing again' — a written diagnosis with no manual entry (verify.json id 8 holds only floor(87/4) = 21 and the remainder 3), and problems 1, 2 and 6 each require drawn work ('Circle groups of 4', 'Rearrange them into rows of 5', 'Draw a ring around one friend's share') that no machine checked either. Second, and specific to a visual-models task: the counter, tile and marble arrays are hand-authored TikZ inside worksheet.tex, and gate_log.txt step 9 says 'no triangle-type or “figure” problems in the JSON — skipping', so nothing compared the drawn quantity to the dividend. I counted them from the source and all three are right (3×9 = 27 counters, 4×9+2 = 38 tiles, 10×7+4 = 74 marbles), so this is a latent gap rather than a present error — but it is precisely the hand-drawn-figure class render_figures.py's own docstring says the pipeline exists to eliminate.

strengths_to_preserve: The sheet is built around one contrast and then pays it off: problem 5 (53 students, 8 per van) needs the leftover rounded UP to a seventh van, problem 10 (96 cm of ribbon, 7 cm per bow) needs the identical arithmetic shape with the leftover dropped, and problem 10's manual entry asks the student to explain the difference. The key states the transferable idea: 'The arithmetic 96 ÷ 7 = 13 R 5 is identical in both stories — what changes is the question.'

Every division in the answer key is closed with the multiply-back identity the worksheet's own directions demand (6×4+3 = 27, 7×5+3 = 38, 9×8+2 = 74, 6×24+1 = 145, 4×21+3 = 87, 5×269+2 = 1347, 7×13+5 = 96), so the check is modelled ten times rather than described once.

Problem 8 teaches the remainder rule as a diagnostic instrument, not a fact: Nia's 20 R 7 is refuted without redividing ('a remainder must be smaller than the divisor, and 7 is bigger than 4'), and the trap value 20 is declared so the key can name what a wrong 20 means.

Problem 7's partial-quotients table gives the intermediate chunk (6 × 20 = 120) on the page and asks the child to finish it, which connects the model to the notation instead of leaving the method implicit.

The study guide's Skill 4 names the three ways a story uses a remainder (round up / drop it / the remainder IS the answer) and its worked example and try-it both land on the round-up case that the worksheet's problem 5 exercises.

root_causes.description: Manual flagging tracked the most conspicuous open item and stopped. Problem 10's compare-the-two-stories explanation was declared; problem 8's 'explain how you can tell she is wrong' was not, because the same problem also asks for a quotient and a remainder that are machine-checkable, and the numeric coverage was read as covering the whole item. The drawn work in problems 1, 2 and 6 is in the same position: the numbers under the picture are verified, the picture the child is told to produce is not recorded anywhere.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 8: 'Use the remainder rule to explain how you can tell she is wrong without dividing again.' verify.json id 8 holds only floor(a/b) = 21 and a - b*floor(a/b) = 3.
worksheet.pdf problem 1 'Circle groups of 4', problem 2 'Rearrange them into rows of 5', problem 6 'Draw a ring around one friend's share' — none has a manual entry.
verify.json declares 'manual' exactly once, on id 10; gate_log.txt reports 'verify-ws MANUAL' with one flagged item.
The prompt requires 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review'.

root_causes.description: The counted-array models carry the problem's principal given (27 counters, 38 tiles, 74 marbles) but live only as hand-written TikZ foreach loops in the worksheet source. The declarative figure pipeline covers triangles and right triangles, so a concept-models task in the number strand falls outside it entirely and the figure gate skips. A miscounted loop bound would ship silently: the JSON would still verify, every gate would still pass, and the picture would contradict the prose.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 1: '\\foreach \\r in {0,1,2} \\foreach \\c in {0,...,8}' — 27 counters, matching 'The counters below show 27'.
worksheet.tex problem 2: 4 rows of 9 plus 2 = 38 tiles; problem 6: 10 rows of 7 plus 4 = 74 marbles. All three counts are correct.

gate_log.txt step 9: 'no triangle-type or “figure” problems in the JSON — skipping'; gate summary 'render-figures SKIPPED(no figure problems)'; step 12 'problem blocks: figure scope ok (none of the 10 problems carries a valued figure)'.

scripts/render_figures.py docstring: figures are constructed from the verify JSON precisely because 'the agent solved the triangle by hand and retyped coordinates into TikZ ... which is exactly the transcription drift verify.py exists to kill'.

improvements.title: Problem 8's written remainder-rule diagnosis and the drawn work in problems 1, 2 and 6 must be declared manual
improvements.proposed_change: Require a manual entry whenever a problem body contains an explanation imperative ('explain', 'say how', 'why', 'describe') or a drawing imperative ('circle', 'ring', 'draw', 'shade', 'mark', 'rearrange ... into'), independently of whether the same problem also carries verified numbers. Enforce it as a gate lint over the worksheet source keyed by problem id, and state the rule in SKILL.md so authors encode it up front. The answer key should then print an acceptance criterion for each, as it already does for problem 10.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with curr-111's problem 8 text and a verify.json holding only the quotient and remainder evals. The lint must exit non-zero naming problem 8's explanation slot; adding {id: 8, type: 'manual', desc: 'Explain, using the remainder rule, how you know 20 R 7 is wrong'} must make it pass. A second fixture with problem 1's 'Circle groups of 4' must behave the same way.
improvements.expected_impact: Raises this sheet's declared manual items from one to at least four, which is what a parent grading a visual-model division sheet actually has to review, and satisfies the prompt's explicit labelling clause.
improvements.risk: Drawing verbs appear in directions blocks and in study-guide prose; the lint must scan problem bodies only, and authors need an explicit way to acknowledge a drawing that is scaffolding rather than a graded response.

improvements.title: Counted-array and bar models should be generated from the verify JSON, not hand-written TikZ that no gate counts
improvements.proposed_change: Extend the declarative figure system beyond triangles with kinds the elementary bands need — e.g. {"kind": "counter_array", "count": 27, "cols": 9} and {"kind": "part_bar", "parts": 8, "shaded": 3} — drawn by scripts/render_figures.py from the same numbers the problem's own check consumes, exactly as triangles already are. Then make the figure-scope rule in tests/check_layout.py fail a problem whose body contains a raw \\begin{tikzpicture} carrying a countable quantity that is not sourced from the JSON, so hand-drawn value-bearing figures cannot pass silently the way they do here.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem states 'The counters below show 27' with a hand-written foreach drawing 26 counters and a verify entry floor(27/4) = 6. The new check must exit non-zero reporting the figure/given mismatch; re-authoring the problem with {"figure": {"kind": "counter_array", "count": 27}} must pass and must emit a probfig macro drawing exactly 27.
improvements.expected_impact: Brings the concept-models band under the same construction guarantee geometry already has, so a drawn count can never disagree with the dividend. On this task the counts are correct, so the gain is eliminating a silent failure mode rather than fixing a present error.
improvements.risk: A new figure kind is new rendering surface with its own layout failure modes (overflow on large counts, column choice); the renderer needs a size cap and a fallback, and existing hand-drawn sheets will need re-authoring before the stricter layout rule can be turned on.

case_summary: A well-designed guided division sheet: quotient-and-remainder language is fixed by the directions, every division is closed by multiplying back, and the whole set is arranged around one contrast — problem 5's leftover students force an extra van while problem 10's leftover ribbon is simply left over — with problem 10's explanation properly declared manual. All ten problems and all eight study-guide values recompute correctly, so the ACCEPT is right. Two gaps the judge did not reach: problem 8's 'explain how you can tell she is wrong' is a written diagnosis with no manual entry, and problems 1, 2 and 6 ask for circled or rearranged groups that nothing records; and the counter, tile and marble arrays are hand-written TikZ outside the declarative figure pipeline, so the gate chain never compared the drawn quantity to the dividend. I counted all three from the source and they are correct, which makes this a latent verification gap rather than a shipped error.
